claims.value: <MaxQuant search>_<strain code>_fr<gradient fraction>, e.g. lepA_3plex1_MRG04_fr07 (437 sources)
claims.evidence: One source per (independent SILAC experiment x strain culture x sucrose-gradient fraction), following curated PXD004650 (fraction-specific source names) and review round 1 finding 2: each gradient fraction is a distinct particle population of that culture. The experiment id is the deposited search/RAW bundle name (lepA_2plex1..rsgA_3plex4); the strain code is the one the SI Methods assign to the SILAC state of that series (light MRG03/MRG06, medium MRG04/MRG07, heavy MRG05/MRG08). Strain codes are evidenced by paper quotes, not inferred.

light-labelled strains MRG03 (lepA series) and MRG06 (rsgA series): SI "MRG03 (WT, wild-type control)", "MRG06 (WT, control)"; "light (unlabeled Arg and Lys; strains MRG03 and MRG06)". 172 rows. Free-text genotype as a custom column (spec README 'Extending Templates' permits custom characteristics; curated PXD004650 carries characteristics[genotype] under ms-proteomics only); ASCII wording chosen instead of the paper's Δ notation.

medium-labelled MRG04: "MRG04 (M, mutant ΔlepA)"; "medium (Arg 13C6 and Lys 2H4; strains MRG04 and MRG07)". 81 rows. Free-text genotype as a custom column (spec README 'Extending Templates' permits custom characteristics; curated PXD004650 carries characteristics[genotype] under ms-proteomics only); ASCII wording chosen instead of the paper's Δ notation.

heavy-labelled MRG05: "MRG05 (C, complemented ΔlepA/lepA+)"; "heavy (Arg 13C6 15N4 and Lys 13C6 15N2; strains MRG05 and MRG08)"; "Plasmid pLEPA was transformed into MRG02 to generate MRG05.". 48 rows. Free-text genotype as a custom column (spec README 'Extending Templates' permits custom characteristics; curated PXD004650 carries characteristics[genotype] under ms-proteomics only); ASCII wording chosen instead of the paper's Δ notation.

medium-labelled MRG07: "MRG07 (M, ΔrsgA)". 91 rows. Free-text genotype as a custom column (spec README 'Extending Templates' permits custom characteristics; curated PXD004650 carries characteristics[genotype] under ms-proteomics only); ASCII wording chosen instead of the paper's Δ notation.

heavy-labelled MRG08: "MRG08 (C, ΔrsgA/rsgA+)". 56 rows. Free-text genotype as a custom column (spec README 'Extending Templates' permits custom characteristics; curated PXD004650 carries characteristics[genotype] under ms-proteomics only); ASCII wording chosen instead of the paper's Δ notation.

claims.value: SILAC light = WT; SILAC medium (Arg6/Lys4) = deletion mutant; SILAC heavy (Arg10/Lys8) = complemented strain
claims.evidence: Explicit label statement in SI Methods (see genotype claims; medium = "Arg 13C6 and Lys 2H4" = MaxQuant Arg6;Lys4, heavy = "Arg 13C6 15N4 and Lys 13C6 15N2" = Arg10;Lys8). Every search's summary.txt lists Labels0 empty (light), Labels1 Arg6;Lys4 and, for 3-plex, Labels2 Arg10;Lys8. Data cross-check (batch rule 6): lepA_3plex1 LepA (P60785) M/L 0.45, H/M 9.0 (mutant channel depleted, complemented channel overexpressed); rsgA_3plex1 RsgA (P39286) M/L 0.18, H/M 11.7; the non-targeted GTPase is flat (RsgA in lepA_3plex1 M/L 1.0). 2-plex searches contain no target-protein group, so the 2-plex map rests on the paper text (same medium label = mutant statement). The 2-plex Arg6;Lys4 state is written 'SILAC medium' (mass/label identity) although MaxQuant names it 'H' in a 2-plex search.

claims.value: SILAC light / SILAC medium (2-plex runs: 2 rows per run)
claims.evidence: multiplicity 2 in summary.txt/mqpar.xml of lepA_2plex1/2 and rsgA_2plex1/2 (136 rows, 68 runs).

claims.value: 1..n per genotype group, unique per independent culture
claims.evidence: Batch rule 3; the number identifies the culture and is shared by all gradient-fraction sources of that culture. Each deposited search = one independent experiment (inferred: the counts match the paper exactly - Fig. 1 'Five independent experiments' = 5 lepA searches; Fig. 3 'Six' = 6 rsgA searches; Fig. S3 complemented ΔlepA 'Three' = 3 lepA 3-plex searches). wild type 1-5 = MRG03 cultures of lepA_2plex1,lepA_2plex2,lepA_3plex1..3; 6-11 = MRG06 cultures of rsgA_2plex1,rsgA_2plex2,rsgA_3plex1..4 (one 'wild type' group because both strains are described as WT controls; numbers kept unique across the 11 cultures). lepA deletion 1-5, lepA complemented 1-3, rsgA deletion 1-6, rsgA complemented 1-4. Re-injections share their culture's number.

SI: strains "were moved by P1 transduction into parental strain BW25113", isogenic Lys- Arg- auxotroph derivatives; NCBITaxon:679895 'Escherichia coli BW25113' verified in OLS. PRIDE organism 'Escherichia coli' and the search FASTA 'uniprot-ecoli+k12' are consistent (BW25113 is a K-12 derivative).

claims.location: characteristics[organism part] / characteristics[cell type] / characteristics[disease] rows 1-448
claims.evidence: Whole bacterial cultures: no anatomy, no cell type distinct from the organism, no disease. Reserved word permitted by the contract for all three columns.

claims.value: deposited MaxQuant search / RAW bundle id (lepA_2plex1 ... rsgA_3plex4)
claims.evidence: Groups the 2 or 3 strain cultures whose gradient fractions were mixed and measured together; equals the deposited <x>txt.zip / <x>-<n>.zip names.

claims.value: Bruker .d folder name inside the deposited ZIP bundle
claims.evidence: PRIDE exposes only 11 RAW ZIP bundles (56-124 GB); their central directories list 172 .d folders, identical 1:1 to the Raw file column of the 11 summary.txt files (0 deposited-not-searched, 0 searched-not-deposited). Following the reviewed PXD004817 precedent, comment[data file] holds the member .d name; the containing ZIP is listed per run in run_fraction.tsv and the report. assay name = .d stem (build default).

claims.location: characteristics[sucrose gradient fraction] and factor value[sucrose gradient fraction] rows 1-448
claims.evidence: Each run is one sucrose-gradient fraction in which the corresponding WT/M/C fractions were mixed ("Twenty-two fractions were collected from each gradient, and equivalent fractions were then combined"; "Corresponding fractions from WT, M, and C strains were mixed"); the paper's readout is the per-fraction M/WT and C/WT ratio profile (Fig. 1 fractions 6-16, Fig. 3 6-18), and MaxQuant ran each fraction as its own Experiment. The number is the MaxQuant 'Experiment' (F1, fr01, Fr02 ...) cross-checked against the run name; rsgA_3plex2-4 cover fractions 6-18 (13 runs each), all other experiments 1-16. Modelled as a sample property and factor (custom column, curated PXD004650 precedent: characteristics[sucrose gradient fraction]) so downstream tools do not merge fractions.
No peptide-level fractionation: each run is one injection of one gradient-fraction sample (build default; no post-build edit).

claims.location: comment[technical replicate] rows 2,19,68,70,72,87,89,91,292,309,326 (=2; all other rows =1)
claims.value: 2 = second injection of an already-measured gradient-fraction sample (same source name)
claims.evidence: 11 rows / 5 runs: JM_KurtF1REDO (lepA_2plex1 F1; MaxQuant puts it as fraction 2 of experiment F1), rsgA2plex-1-F01/F02/F03-redo (fractions 1-3 also deposited as originals), rsgA3plex-1-F11-redo (F11 original also deposited). Runs named redo/repeat whose original was NOT deposited (lepA_3plex1 fr11-redo, lepA_3plex3 f01/f02redo, rsgA_2plex2 F15-redo, rsgA_3plex1 F12-F14-redo, rsgA_3plex3 fr17repeat) are the only injection of that fraction and stay technical replicate 1.

SI "a quadrupole–time of flight mass spectrometer (Impact II; Bruker Daltonics)"; every .d contains microTOFQImpactAcquisition.method and 'nlc impact ii system 2.hss'; mqpar msInstrument=1 (Bruker Q-TOF). PRIDE's 'Bruker Daltonics instrument model' is only the generic parent.
MaxQuant summary.txt reports MS/MS spectra identified per run from a standard (non-DIA) SILAC search; the method is a Bruker auto MS/MS ('m4-mann.m') method. No DIA settings anywhere.

Impact II Q-TOF fragments in its quadrupole collision cell; the acquisition method carries Collision_* cell parameters and CollisionEnergy settings, no ETD/ECD. Inferred from instrument architecture + method parameters, not stated in prose.
Q-TOF: MS/MS read out by the TOF analyzer; MaxQuant used its TOF MS/MS parameter set (40 ppm).
parameters.txt of all 11 searches: 'MS/MS tol. (TOF) 40 ppm'; mqpar.xml msmsParams Name=TOF MatchTolerance 40, MatchToleranceInPpm=true.
mqpar.xml mainSearchTol (0.006, searchTolInPpm=false) for lepA_2plex1; 34 rows.
mqpar.xml mainSearchTol (10, searchTolInPpm=true) for rsgA_3plex2, rsgA_3plex3, rsgA_3plex4; 117 rows.

All 11 searches: Enzyme 'Trypsin/P', specific, 2 missed cleavages. Batch rule 2 records the digestion enzyme (Trypsin) not the search rule (Trypsin/P, MS:1001313). The paper only says bands were "digested out of the gel as described" (Chan et al. 2006); trypsin is therefore inferred from the search, which is the standard of that cited Foster-lab in-gel protocol.

Labels written MT=Variable (batch rule 11).

claims.value: Label:13C(6)15N(4) R (UNIMOD:267) Variable; Label:13C(6)15N(2) K (UNIMOD:259) Variable
claims.evidence: 3-plex searches only: Labels2 'Arg10;Lys8' (= paper "Arg 13C6 15N4 and Lys 13C6 15N2"). 312 rows.

claims.location: technology type / comment[sdrf template] / comment[sdrf annotation tool] / comment[sdrf version] rows 1-448
claims.value: proteomic profiling by mass spectrometry; NT=ms-proteomics;VV=v1.2.0; NT=sdrf-skills;VV=v0.1.0; v1.1.0
claims.evidence: Batch rules 1 and 10. ms-proteomics latest 1.2.0 per upstream sdrf-templates 7da1747 templates.yaml:150 (the spec submodule's nested templates copy is older). No organism template applies to bacteria (human/vertebrates/invertebrates/plants are all eukaryote-specific). Only ms-proteomics is declared (review round 1 finding 1: clinical-metadata dropped); characteristics[genotype] and characteristics[sucrose gradient fraction] are custom columns per the spec's 'Extending Templates' section, as in curated PXD004650 and the curated E. coli SDRFs, which all declare ms-proteomics only.

limitations: Paper full text is not open access in PMC/Europe PMC (fullTextXML HTTP 500, supplementaryFiles 'not open access', efetch front matter only, PNAS/Unpaywall PDF HTTP 403, PMC HTML behind reCAPTCHA for curl). Methods/SI were read through WebFetch of the PMC page, which passes text through a summarising model; only its short exact quotations (evidence/paper_quotes.txt) were used for values. A reviewer with institutional access should confirm the SI strain table and label sentence.

techsdrf is not installed; instrument/activation were read from range-extracted .d method files (SampleInfo.xml, microTOFQImpactAcquisition.method) of one run only (JM_KurtF1_B8_01_1123.d), not from every run; analysis.baf headers were not parsed.

comment[precursor mass tolerance] is 'not available' for 7 of 11 searches (297 of 448 rows): only lepA_2plex1 (0.006 Da) and rsgA_3plex2/3/4 (10 ppm) deposited mqpar.xml, parameters.txt does not record it, and the two recorded values differ, so neither is extrapolated. Consequence: parse_sdrf convert-openms refuses the file as is.

Digestion enzyme is not named in the paper (in-gel digestion 'as described', Chan et al. 2006); Trypsin is taken from the search (Trypsin/P). Reduction and alkylation reagents are unstated: 'not available' (Carbamidomethyl fixed in the search implies alkylation, the reagent is unknown).

No ontology term exists for sucrose-density-gradient fractionation under PRIDE:0000550 (children: off-gel electrophoresis, isoelectric focusing, HPLC, gel electrophoresis), so comment[fractionation method] is omitted; the short SDS-PAGE run was a clean-up, not fractionation. The gradient fraction is a sample property (characteristics[sucrose gradient fraction], custom column) and a factor; comment[fraction identifier] = 1.

The SDRF is the byte-identical concatenation of two sdrf-tools build outputs (2-plex and 3-plex searches, identical headers; batch rule 5) by scratch tools/assemble.py, which edits no cell. A single build cannot emit both because technical.tsv holds one constant modification set.

One independent experiment per deposited search is inferred from the matching counts (5/6/3) in the figure legends, not stated per file. MRG03 and MRG06 are both written 'wild type'; whether they differ (e.g. vector) is not stated in the quoted text.
Strain-level genotype details reported only by the WebFetch summary (pWSK29 empty vector, ΔlysA::kan argE::Tn10 markers) were not written to the SDRF.

The 2-plex channel map (light WT / medium mutant) cannot be checked against the data: neither LepA nor RsgA is quantified in the 2-plex proteinGroups.txt files examined (lepA_2plex1, rsgA_2plex1); it rests on the paper's label statement.
Review hand-off: external sdrf-adversarial-review requested by the caller (REVIEW_PENDING_EXTERNAL); no reviewer dispatched and no review-gate run in this task.
